strengths: Novel and well-motivated approach using Fourier features grounded in interpretability findings (Zhou et al. 2024)
Solid mathematical foundation with rigorous lemmas justifying digit recovery via modular arithmetic
Comprehensive experimental methodology with extensive ablations on synthetic arithmetic tasks
Impressive quantitative results: 64× data efficiency, 3-6× token reduction, perfect accuracy on multiple benchmarks
Strong reproducibility with detailed algorithms, clear experimental setup, and thorough appendix
Evidence of real-model integration: continual pretraining on Llama-3.1 without harming semantics; FineWeb pretraining maintains/improves language modeling
Systematic evaluation across model sizes, data regimes, and architectural variations
weaknesses: Evaluation almost exclusively on synthetic arithmetic tasks; no assessment on standard quantitative reasoning benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K, DROP)
Real-world applicability unclear: continual pretraining on Llama shows modest improvements (4-digit addition: 51.35% → 59.00%), not transformative
Theoretical-practice gap: Lemma D.2 assumes orthogonality not guaranteed in practice; decoding uses approximate argmax without error characterization
Limited scope of synthetic evaluation: tasks restricted to 6 digits primarily (except 60-digit addition at 97.42% accuracy); no systematic out-of-distribution robustness analysis
Float64 precision limits (15 digits) inadequately addressed; chunking solution adds complexity and is only evaluated up to 60 digits
Incomplete baseline comparisons: XVAL achieves 0.44% on decimal addition (seems suspiciously low); limited comparison with recent methods; fine-tuned Llama comparison conflates model size and method
Design choice justifications incomplete: Why 2 dimensions per digit? Base-10 period choice justified primarily by prior empirical observations, not fundamental principles
No evaluation of robustness to malformed numbers, scientific notation, negative numbers, or real-world number distributions (violates uniform sampling assumptions)
Missing standard ablations: sensitivity to embedding dimension d, effect of non-power-of-10 periods, alternative decoding strategies
Weak evidence that improved arithmetic translates to better downstream task performance on real-world quantitative reasoning

strengths: Mathematically principled approach using modular Fourier encodings with clear theoretical justification (Lemmas 3.3-3.4)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on synthetic arithmetic tasks with strong empirical results (100% accuracy, 64× data efficiency gains)
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (periods, linear layers, necessity of sine/cosine)
Well-written with detailed algorithms and appendices supporting reproducibility
Addresses a real limitation of LLMs—poor arithmetic performance despite scale
weaknesses: Severely limited real-world evaluation: only synthetic pure-arithmetic tasks. No evaluation on math reasoning benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K), quantitative QA, or other downstream tasks where numerical reasoning matters
Integration with actual LLMs is weak and unconvincing. Continual pretraining on Llama-3.1-1B (Table 4) shows only 8-10% improvements on arithmetic and no MMLU improvement (38.10% → 38.21%)

Fundamental practicality issues: requires retraining LLMs from scratch; breaks existing tokenization; incompatible with pre-trained models. Simplified FoNE (for continual pretraining) operates on top of BPE, contradicting core single-token claims

Gap between theory and practice: Lemmas establish what information can be recovered, but provide no guarantee that transformers will learn the heuristic decoding procedure (Definition 3.7). No analysis of when dot-product similarity might fail
The 'single-token' claim is misleading for long numbers: numbers >15 digits require chunking (Section 5); 60-digit addition achieves 97.42% (not 100%) and performance degrades with length

Unfair comparisons: fine-tuned Llama-3.2-1B compared against models trained from scratch; XVAL shows suspiciously low performance (0.44%) suggesting implementation issues; missing comparison with concurrent methods (Zausinger et al. 2024)

Limited novelty: sinusoidal encodings date to Vaswani et al. 2017; core contribution (applying known Fourier features to number tokens) is straightforward once you know LLMs learn such features (Zhou et al. 2024)

Insufficient failure analysis: no investigation of when/why FoNE underperforms; limited exploration of out-of-distribution generalization; no zero-shot transfer studies; unclear why period selection is critical (Table 3)

Technical concerns with decoding: independent digit classification (Definition 3.6) doesn't model carrying or arithmetic constraints; unclear how model learns that 9+1=10 with independent decoders; no empirical analysis of logit distributions

Weak real-world validation: Table 5 shows FoNE doesn't hurt FineWeb pretraining but doesn't demonstrate benefits; WikiTableQuestions mentioned but not evaluated; no evidence FoNE helps with numerical aspects of reasoning (MMLU unchanged)

strengths: Clear problem motivation addressing two key limitations of standard number tokenization: frequency bias and token fragmentation
Strong theoretical foundation with rigorous lemmas proving numeracy preservation under layer/RMS normalization using modular arithmetic
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on multiple arithmetic tasks with appropriate baselines (digit-wise, subword, XVAL) and thorough ablations validating design choices
Impressive empirical results: 100% accuracy on multiple tasks, 64× data efficiency gain, 3-6× token reduction, and outperformance of fine-tuned Llama-3.2-1B with 38M parameters
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithms, experimental setup, and multiple appendices enabling replication
Practical compatibility demonstrated through integration with Abacus method, handling of 60-digit numbers, and continual pretraining on existing LLMs
weaknesses: Evaluation scope is narrow: primarily focuses on synthetic arithmetic tasks without sufficient validation of claimed applicability to broader numerical reasoning (mathematical theorems, physics laws, complex QA)

Real-world impact on large models unclear: main results on modest-scale models (38M-117M); continual pretraining on Llama-3.1-1B shows only modest improvements (e.g., 4-digit addition 51.35%→59%) and MMLU unchanged
Generalization concerns: base-10 design appears empirical; float64 15-digit limit requires chunking workaround adding complexity; limited analysis of extrapolation beyond training distribution

Weak language modeling evaluation: Table 5 perplexity improvements marginal and not clearly significant; Table 4 shows no semantic improvement (MMLU 38.10%→38.21%), undermining claims of preserving semantic abilities
Decoding mechanism may be brittle: relies on exact digit classification via circular embeddings without error analysis; error propagation through aggregation not studied
Hyperparameter selection lack guidance: global m,n parameters require per-dataset tuning with no principled selection method provided for practitioners
Important justifications relegated to discussion section (Q1-Q3) rather than main text; integration procedure could clarify [NUM] token semantics better
